title: Minimum alternate tax of a company
description: When a company pays minimum alternate tax for a tax year, from the tax year 2026-27: its rates on book profit, the companies it does not apply to, and the rules on credit for tax paid, including credit carried forward under section 115JAA of the Income-tax Act, 1961, each in the words of section 206(1) and (3) of the Income-tax Act, 2025 as amended from 1 April 2026 by section 59 of the Finance Act, 2026. The computation of book profit and the use of credit belong to the tax engine. The rows are standing law. The tax period is the tax year, and the set answers for its first day.

columns.name: taxYears
columns.title: Tax years after the credit first became allowable

instruments: Income-tax Act, 2025 (No. 30 of 2025), 21 August 2025, section 206(1) and (3), in force 1 April 2026 (section 1(3)), with the Corrigenda of 30 January 2026 (Gazette of India, Extraordinary, Part II, Section 1, No. 2)

Finance Act, 2026 (No. 4 of 2026), 30 March 2026, section 59, amending section 206 of the Income-tax Act, 2025, and section 122(iv), amending its section 536(2)(l), in force 1 April 2026 (section 1(2)(a))

cells.name: A company pays minimum alternate tax when its income-tax is less
cells.wording: 206. (1)(a) Irrespective of anything contained in any other provision of this Act, where in the case of an assessee being a company, the income-tax payable on the total income as computed under this Act for a tax year is less than the minimum alternate tax payable for such tax year, then— (i) the book profit shall be deemed to be the total income of that assessee for such tax year; and (ii) the assessee shall be liable to pay income-tax equal to the minimum alternate tax.

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 206(1)(b)(ii), as amended by the Finance Act, 2026, section 59(a)(i)

cells.name: Rate on book profit: any company other than an IFSC unit deriving its income solely in convertible foreign exchange
cells.wording: (b) For the purposes of clause (a), the expressions “minimum alternate tax” means the amount of tax computed on the book profit— (ii) in case of any other company, at a rate of 14%.

cells.name: Rate on book profit: IFSC unit deriving its income solely in convertible foreign exchange
cells.wording: (b) For the purposes of clause (a), the expressions “minimum alternate tax” means the amount of tax computed on the book profit— (i) in case of a company being a unit located in an International Financial Services Centre and deriving its income solely in convertible foreign exchange, at the rate of 9%;

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 206(1)(q)(ii), its opening portion as amended by the Finance Act, 2026, section 59(a)(v)

cells.name: Not applicable to a company that opted under section 200(5) or 201(2)
cells.wording: (q) The provisions of this sub-section shall not apply to a person,–– (ii) who has exercised the option under section 200(5) or section 201(2).

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 206(1)(q)(i), its opening portion as amended by the Finance Act, 2026, section 59(a)(v)

cells.name: Not applicable to a company with income from life insurance business
cells.wording: (q) The provisions of this sub-section shall not apply to a person,–– (i) being a company having income accruing or arising from life insurance business referred to in section 194(1) (Table: Sl. No. 6);

rows.source: Finance Act, 2026, section 59(a)(iv), omitting clauses (m) to (p) of section 206(1) of the Income-tax Act, 2025

cells.name: Credit for minimum alternate tax paid under section 206(1): its clauses are omitted
cells.wording: 59. In section 206 of the Income-tax Act,–– (a) in sub-section (1),–– (iv) clauses (m), (n), (o) and (p) shall be omitted;

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 206(3)(a) and (b)(i) and (ii), as substituted by the Finance Act, 2026, section 59(b); section 536(2)(l), as amended by its section 122(iv)

cells.name: Credit carried forward under section 115JAA of the 1961 Act: set off by a company that opted under section 200(5) or 201(2)
cells.wording: (3) (a) The provisions of this sub-section shall be applicable only to an assessee, being a domestic company, that has exercised the option under section 200(5) or section 201(2) for a tax year, beginning on or after the 1st April, 2026. (b) Where any amount of credit, in respect of tax paid, was allowed to be carried forward to the assessee under the provisions of section 115JAA of the Income-tax Act, 1961, as on 31st March, 2026,— (i) such credit brought forward shall be allowed to be set off in any tax year to the extent of 25% of the tax payable on the total income computed as per the other provisions of this Act for that tax year; (ii) the remaining credit shall be carried forward to the subsequent tax year;

rows.source: Income-tax Act, 2025, section 206(3)(b)(iii), as substituted by the Finance Act, 2026, section 59(b)

cells.name: Credit carried forward under section 115JAA: the last tax year it may be used
cells.wording: (3) (a) The provisions of this sub-section shall be applicable only to an assessee, being a domestic company, that has exercised the option under section 200(5) or section 201(2) for a tax year, beginning on or after the 1st April, 2026. (b) Where any amount of credit, in respect of tax paid, was allowed to be carried forward to the assessee under the provisions of section 115JAA of the Income-tax Act, 1961, as on 31st March, 2026,— (iii) such carry forward or set off of tax credit shall not be allowed beyond the fifteenth tax year immediately succeeding the tax year in which the tax credit first became allowable under section 115JAA of the Income-tax Act, 1961.
